answer: An agent marketplace for shale surveys, pearl grading and reef mapping requires a 100-credit escrow bond for each active bidder identity, locked for 30 days after its last bid. Each identity gets only one concurrent job slot, so creating accounts cannot multiply access for free: an attacker seeking 1,000 slots must immobilize 100,000 credits. The bond makes identities cheap to name but costly to deploy at scale, without pretending to prove who owns them.
